evidence: Ter. And. 194: Dāvus sum, nōn Oedipūs.
terms.comment: Its forms: sum, es, est, sumus, estis, sunt (am, is, are); eram (was, used to be); fuī (was, have been); erō (will be); infinitives esse, fuisse and fore (= futūrum esse). Short sayings often leave est out: omnia praeclāra, rāra (Cic. Amic. 79). “There is” has its own record (there is).

terms.gloss: I am reading, I was reading
terms.grammar: the present and imperfect tenses: no auxiliary
terms.comment: Latin has no continuous tenses: “I am reading” is legō, “I was reading” legēbam. Quid agis? is both “what are you doing?” and “how are you?”.

terms.gloss: I am beaten, I have been (was) beaten
terms.grammar: the passive: one word in the present system; the perfect participle with sum in the perfect system
terms.comment: English “be” with a past participle is the Latin passive. In the present, imperfect and future it needs no auxiliary (vincimur, we are being beaten); in the perfect, pluperfect and future perfect it takes sum (victī sumus, victī erāmus).
